evaluator: Fictionalized Margaret Morse analytical lens only. I am not Margaret Morse, do not speak for her, and this is not an endorsement.
evidence: The homepage immediately identifies Jamie as a Technical Project Manager focused on Product Operations and Implementation and presents the recurring usable-systems method.
Within one click, About makes the artistic, civic, technical, and social lineage explicit through Open House, WOW List, Sunday Dinner and 196, NYC Artist Coalition, and source-backed team memory.
About presents three bounded systems loops through relationships, model, interface and use, and learning and continuity.
FairRentNYC connects facilitated gatherings, campaign sites, public pathways, sources, minutes, question logs, and handoffs while separating Jamie's role from collective outcomes.
WOW List shows community language becoming a natural-language collaborative platform while crediting Richard Caceres and the organizer community.
Sunday Dinner and 196 make hospitality, onboarding, artist support, recurring gatherings, and documentation into participation infrastructure while withholding participant records.
Dates and statuses are bounded, and source notes are usable rather than decorative.
safety_findings: The portfolio distinguishes individual contribution from collective authorship and policy causation.
Participant privacy is treated as a design constraint.
No private correspondence, participant-level records, access instructions, stakeholder lists, or unapproved testimonials were encountered.
recommendation: PASS. Within two clicks, the portfolio makes Jamie's inhabited-systems practice and target role legible across more than three accurately bounded examples.
